content:
The first Home Ownership Scheme (HOS) flat built using the "Modular Integrated Construction" (MiC) method, On Pak Court in Kwun Tong, has been occupied for only 15 months. Recently, owners have reported that the exterior wall paint is peeling, blistering, flaking off, and even growing moss. "集誌社" (FactWire) inspected the site on Thursday (the 8th) and found workers on suspended platforms painting at several locations, with no blistering visible on the exterior walls. However, the adjacent On Wa Court, also built using MiC, shows large-scale blistering on its exterior walls similar to On Pak Court, and multiple cracks have appeared on the estate's boundary wall, with efflorescence seeping out. Some residents are worried that problems will persist after the Housing Department's maintenance period expires, forcing owners to pool funds for repairs, and bluntly stated, "Spent millions on a defective building," hoping the Housing Department will maintain the estate's common areas permanently.

On Pak Court and the adjacent On Wa Court are the first HOS projects of the Housing Department to adopt the MiC construction method, in which residential units are prefabricated in mainland factories, with structure, plumbing, electrical and interior decoration completed, before being transported to Hong Kong for assembly into buildings.

Blistering on exterior walls of On Wa Court

"集誌社" (FactWire) arrived at Anderson Road this afternoon to inspect. The repair work on the exterior walls of On Pak Court was largely completed, while water seepage marks and cracks remained on the estate's boundary wall. However, the exterior walls of On Wa Court, also built using MiC and located across a street, showed similar problems. On one exterior wall, the entire 28-storey surface was blistered, and the joints between floors were noticeably uneven. Multiple fine diagonal cracks were visible on the estate's boundary wall, with efflorescence seeping out, leaving white crystals on the surface. Mr and Mrs Cheung, residents of On Wa Court, said they had only moved in two months ago, with no leakage inside their unit, but they had noticed paint peeling and flaking on the orange-coloured parts of the exterior walls.

Recently, some On Pak Court owners reported to the media that there had been numerous complaints in residents' group chats about ongoing leaks since occupancy. Some found water seepage in the kitchen and bathroom upon taking possession of their units, with extensive blistering and flaking on the building's walls, and moss growing due to water seepage from external wall pipes. Others reported cracks on the high-rise exterior walls and shrinkage cracks in the sealing strips between assembled units.

Leaking toilet pipe discovered

Ms Wong, an On Pak Court resident who took possession of her flat about half a year ago, told "集誌社" (FactWire) that a leaking toilet pipe was discovered at handover and repaired by the contractor, with no subsequent leakage issues inside the unit. However, she was dissatisfied that the new building's paint was already flaking after just one year of occupancy, and worried about further problems after the maintenance period expired, saying, "What if owners have to pool funds for major repairs?" Ms Wong hoped the Housing Department would "guarantee quality to the end" and permanently handle repairs to common areas. She added that workers on suspended platforms had been carrying out repairs at the estate recently, and paint had splattered onto her laundry, forcing her to dry clothes indoors. She bluntly said, "Spent millions on a defective building."

Eaves canopy developed cracks shortly after

Another owner, Ms Tsang, moved in at the beginning of this year. The eaves canopy developed cracks shortly after and was repaired by the contractor, though it is uncertain whether cracks will reappear in "wind and rain." She pointed out that fortunately, the owners were united enough to contact the District Council and the media for follow-up, which forced the Housing Department to carry out repairs. She was not currently worried about having to bear high maintenance costs in the future.

On Wa Court was built by Shui On Construction and completed in August last year, with residents moving in in November. On Wa Court has two blocks providing 990 units, ranging from 296 to 495 square feet, with an average price per square foot of HK$7,030 and unit prices ranging from HK$1.81 million to HK$3.77 million. On Pak Court, built by the same contractor as a simultaneous project, began foundation work in February 2022 and was completed three years later. It is a single block with 420 units, with usable areas ranging from 291 to 498 square feet, an average price of HK$7,000 per square foot, and prices ranging from HK$1.77 million to HK$3.73 million, with residents moving in gradually from July last year.

The Housing Department earlier replied to the media that after receiving complaints about On Pak Court in late July this year, it immediately urged the contractor to carry out comprehensive repairs. Following a drone survey, it was estimated that dust had not been thoroughly cleaned before painting at certain exterior wall locations, or the primer had not been applied evenly, which was attributed to faulty painting workmanship.

In addition, the department did not find any cracks in the walls and believed they were merely water stains on the exterior walls after rain. As for claims that "MiC module sealing strips had shrunk and cracked," the Housing Department confirmed after on-site verification and review of records that this was not the situation described by the owner, but rather a workmanship defect caused by paint spilling onto the sealing strips during wall painting. Cleaning and repairs at that location have been completed, and there is no leakage in the unit.
